claim.pdf_says: ACCEPT Format 3 exception phrase, printed as a BRACKET WITH CHOICE INDICATORS: '⎡|  ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1  |⎤' over '⎣|  NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2  |⎦'. Verified by cropping and enlarging spec_p607.png: a vertical bar sits immediately inside the opening bracket and a matching bar immediately inside the closing bracket, spanning both stacked rows.
claim.why_it_matters: Without the bars a bracket around stacked alternatives means AT MOST ONE of them. Per 5.2.6.4, bars inside a bracket mean zero or more, each at most once, in any order -- so a single ACCEPT screen statement may carry BOTH ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION, in either order. The markdown makes legal source look illegal. Every sibling figure in this batch with the same phrase (613 ADD, 618 CALL Fmt 1, 619 CALL Fmt 2, 640 DISPLAY, 644 DIVIDE) preserves the bars, so 607 is the sole holdout.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent inspection of the printed glyphs, not by trusting the claim. Rendered page 607 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v607/spec_p607.png, 2550x3300) and cropped the exception-phrase delimiters at 8x (crop_left.png = original box 355,1070-440,1275; crop_right.png = 1290,1070-1375,1275).

WHAT I SEE, LEFT EDGE: two distinct strokes separated by clear white space. The inner-left stroke is an opening square bracket -- a vertical spine with a short horizontal serif at the top and another at the bottom, both turning RIGHT. Immediately to its right, and clearly detached from it, stands a plain vertical bar with NO serif at either end, and it is visibly TALLER than the bracket, spanning both stacked rows. RIGHT EDGE: the mirror image -- a plain serif-less vertical bar, then white space, then a closing square bracket whose top and bottom serifs turn LEFT. So the printed delimiter is unambiguously '[|' ... '|]', a bracket enclosing a pair of choice indicators. It is not a thick bracket spine (the bar is detached and unserifed) and not a nested '[[ ]]' (a nested bracket would carry serifs).

WHAT THE MARKDOWN HAS: page-607.md line 10 and specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25265 are byte-identical to the quoted string. The array preamble is {l} -- a single left-aligned column with no vertical rule -- and there is no '|' or \vert anywhere in the expression. The bars are genuinely absent, not reflowed, wrapped, or moved to an adjacent line.

SEMANTIC IMPACT CONFIRMED AGAINST THE SPEC, NOT ASSUMED: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2700 (5.2.6.4) reads verbatim, 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, zero or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' A plain bracket over stacked alternatives instead permits at most one. So the transcription downgrades 'both phrases, either order' to 'at most one phrase', which would make the ordinary ACCEPT screen-name ON EXCEPTION ... NOT ON EXCEPTION ... END-ACCEPT construct read as illegal. That is a normative meaning change, not formatting.

SIBLING COROBORATION CHECKED: grep for 'ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1' in specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns line 25265 (this figure, plain bracket) plus lines 25695, 25732, 26506, 29816, 30635, 30652 -- every one of which uses the '⎡|' ... '|⎤' form. Page anchors place 25265 inside page 607 (anchor at 25256, next page anchor 613 at 25451). Page 644 DIVIDE Format 1 likewise prints '⎡|  ON SIZE ERROR ... |⎤'. Line 25265 is indeed the sole holdout.
verdict.corrected_description:
The finding is real and the core of the description is accurate; two refinements.

(1) Sibling wording is loose. Pages 613 (ADD) and 644 (DIVIDE) do not carry the 'same phrase' -- they carry ON SIZE ERROR / NOT ON SIZE ERROR, not ON EXCEPTION. They are the same STRUCTURAL idiom (an exception phrase pair wrapped in a bracket with choice indicators) and they do preserve the bars, so they still corroborate; the phrase-level claim is just imprecise. The true same-phrase siblings are 618 CALL Fmt 1, 619 CALL Fmt 2, 640 DISPLAY, and the occurrences at ISO_COBOL.md lines 29816, 30635, 30652.

(2) The defect on page 607 is BROADER than the claim states, and the fix should cover both figures. The AT phrase directly above it (page-607.md line 8 / ISO_COBOL.md line 25264) has the identical defect with BRACES instead of brackets. Cropping the AT delimiters at 5x (crop_at_left.png = 450,580-580,1070; crop_at_right.png = 1350,580-1480,1070) shows an opening brace '{' followed by a detached, serif-less vertical bar, and on the right a detached vertical bar followed by '}' and then the outer ']'. The printed form is '[ AT {| [LINE NUMBER ...] / [{COLUMN|COL} NUMBER ...] |} ]'. The markdown renders it as \left\{ ... \right\} with no bars. Per 5.2.6.4, braces WITH choice indicators mean one or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order; braces WITHOUT them mean exactly one. The transcription therefore also makes the everyday 'AT LINE NUMBER 5 COLUMN NUMBER 10' form look illegal, permitting only LINE or only COLUMN. Both figures on page 607 lost their choice indicators and both should be repaired in the same edit, ideally with a figure-notes block matching the style used at ISO_COBOL.md line 25738.
